items.q: A small piece of a message sent over a network is a…
A machine that passes packets along the way is a…
A photo is sent over the internet. Which is true?
choices: it travels in one big piece from start to end
it goes through one single wire all the way
it is drawn again by hand at the other end
it is cut into packets that may take different roads
items.why: A big photo is cut into small numbered packets, and each packet can take its own road through the routers to the other end.

items.q: Packets arrive in the order 3, 1, 2. What does the receiving device do?
choices: uses the numbers to put them back in order
prints them in the order they came
items.why: Every packet carries a number. The receiving device reads the numbers and puts the packets back as 1, 2, 3.

items.q: A road in the network closes while a message is being sent. What happens?
items.why: The network has many roads. When one closes, the routers send the packets along another road, and the message still arrives.

items.q: Information that only you and your family should know is…

items.why: Four random words make a long passphrase that is hard to guess. A name, a birthday or password1 is easy to guess.

items.q: Who may you tell your passphrase?
choices: a parent or another trusted adult only
your best friend, if they promise
a prize team that messages you online
items.why: Your passphrase stays secret, even from your best friend. Only a parent or another trusted adult may know it.

items.q: Why keep a backup copy of your photos somewhere safe?
choices: so they load faster on the tablet
if the tablet breaks you still have them
because the law says you must
so your friends can see them all
items.why: A backup is a spare copy kept somewhere else. If the tablet breaks or gets lost, your photos are still safe.

items.q: A message that tries to trick you into giving away private information is…
choices: a backup copy of a message
a packet on its way to you

items.q: "You won a tablet! Reply with your password to claim it." What do you do?
choices: do not reply, and tell a trusted adult
items.why: A prize you never tried to win and a request for your password are clues of a trick. Do not reply, and tell a trusted adult.

items.q: Which is a sign of a trick message?
choices: it comes from your class page
it says hurry and asks for your passphrase
items.why: Hurry plus a request for your passphrase are two clues of a trick. A short message or one with no pictures can be perfectly safe.

items.q: Why does a cipher wheel keep a message private?
choices: only someone with the key can read it
items.why: The wheel shifts every letter by the key. Only someone who knows the key can turn the letters back and read it.
